components.gap: Construction or argument incomplete for a promised case (unstated assumption). The Poisson and gamma conclusions are asserted for positive real n tending to infinity (body 40-41, 53-56; annex 38-39, 50), and the proof obtains them, including the uniform-on-compacts versions, by applying 'the preceding lemma' / 'the same lemma' (annex 42-43, 52-53). That lemma, thm:p15-feller-concentration, is stated only for families indexed by positive integers n (body 17). No step extends it to real-indexed families (by reindexing along real sequences tending to infinity, or by restating its estimate for an arbitrary law with mean theta and variance v), so the real-n case rests on the lemma outside its stated hypothesis.

defect_observations.observation: Queue destination record is stale: the body now hashes 114178f2... (queue records 6721818a...) and runs to line 377 (queue body_lines end at 366). Cross-reference sentences were inserted at lines 105-107, 349-351 and 362-366, so queue body_lines for C006 onward are shifted; evidence above cites current lines.
Kernel-examples proof applies the integer-indexed concentration lemma (body line 17) to real n; scored as the C002 gap.

The sentence saying the proof uses the integrable symmetrization identity with unbounded integrand 'as required by Exercises 4.7.4-4.7.5' misdescribes the Exercise 4.7.4 part, whose written proof (annex 495-509) uses truncation and the bounded conditional-product identity; only the pair-statistic part (annex 511-519) uses the integrable identity.

The extra identification/uniqueness claim in the finite-urn proof rests on 'the measurable-section strong-law argument used for the Polya mixture' (written in handbook/annex/p15/polya-urns-and-beta-prediction.tex for a beta parameter) rather than written steps or a cited theorem for a general parameter law. The entry's promised content (existence, as in Durrett's post-4.7.10 discussion) does not depend on it, so it was not scored as a gap.

Exchangeability of the Polya urn is obtained by 'the same numerator-permutation argument as in the direct urn proof'; the identical conclusion is stated in thm:p15-polya-word-law (handbook/parts/p15/polya-urns-and-beta-prediction.tex 71-72) and should be cited instead of reused by reference.
Unlabelled reference to 'the conditional-kernel integration theorem'; the matching result is thm:p15-kernel-expectation (handbook/parts/p15/regular-conditional-laws.tex 55-67).

In-proof reuse 'The same lambda-system argument, now starting from the measurable evaluations' (C010) and 'The same last argument shows' (annex 360-361, C011): the reused steps are written immediately above with the substitution named, so they were not scored as unwritten.

The clarification that the three-way equality is not literal equality of unaugmented sigma-fields, and the tail-inclusion facts re-proved in C002 (annex 16-24), duplicate thm:p15-permutation-structure (handbook/parts/p15/limsup-events-and-zero-one-laws.tex 214-227) without citing it or its worked strict-inclusion example (handbook/annex/p15/limsup-events-and-zero-one-laws.tex 350-358).

'This preserves the source Example 4.7.4 argument': the annex (144-145) identifies the limit through the reverse-average Hewitt-Savage theorem, whereas Durrett (p. 251) invokes his Theorem 2.5.4; the reverse-martingale route is otherwise the source's.

The scope boundary neither supplies nor dispositions two remarks inside the cited extent: Feller p. 228 on inequalities from finitely many moments (with footnote 3 references) and p. 229 on applying laws of large numbers and the central limit theorem to exchangeable variables (problem 21 of VIII,10). They are not listed components of these units.
